Comments that appear after the last code token in a file 2. Files that contain only comments (no code tokens) **Example from issue:** Line 18 with `//-- Устарело_Производство21` was triggering `SpaceAtStartComment` diagnostic even though line 1 had `// BSLLS-off`. ## Root Cause 1. The `DiagnosticIgnoranceComputer.computeCommentsIgnorance()` method was calculating the end of ignore ranges using only the last **code** token line. When comments appeared after the last code statement, they fell outside the ignore range. 2. When a file contained only comments (no code tokens), the `compute()` method would return early without processing any ignore directives in those comments. ## Solution 1. Modified the calculation of the last line to consider both the last code token line and the last comment line 2. Changed the early return condition to check if both `codeTokens` and `comments` are empty 3. Pass the comments list to `computeCommentsIgnorance()` to avoid fetching it twice 4. Handle the case when `codeTokens` is empty by using only the last comment line 5. Use `0` instead of `lastCodeTokenLine` when `comments.isEmpty()` for better semantic clarity ## Code Changes **Single file modified:** `DiagnosticIgnoranceComputer.java` - Modified `compute()` to check both codeTokens and comments before early return - Modified `computeCommentsIgnorance()` to accept comments as parameter and handle empty codeTokens - Use `0` for `lastCommentLine` when there are no comments (cleaner semantics) ## Test Coverage Added three comprehensive test cases: 1. `testDiagnosticIgnoranceLastLine()` - Simple case with comment after code 2. `testDiagnosticIgnoranceIssue()` - Exact scenario from the issue with preprocessor directives 3. `testDiagnosticIgnoranceOnlyComments()` - Edge case with only comments in file ## Test Results ✅ All 5 DiagnosticIgnoranceComputerTest tests pass ✅ All 5 SpaceAtStartCommentDiagnosticTest tests pass ✅ All project tests pass ## Impact This fix ensures that diagnostic ignore directives work correctly for: - All comments in a file, regardless of their position relative to code tokens - Files that contain only comments without any code The change is minimal, safe, and preserves all existing behavior while fixing both the reported issue and edge cases identified in code review.

This PR introduces a comprehensive preset management system that revolutionizes how users configure and switch between server contexts. The system provides both interactive TUI and command-line interfaces for creating dynamic server selections.

## Key Features

### New CLI Commands
- **`preset create`** - Command-line preset creation with filter expressions
- **`preset edit`** - Interactive editing with visual server selection
- **`preset list`** - Display all presets in formatted table
- **`preset show`** - Show detailed preset information
- **`preset url`** - Generate client URLs for presets
- **`preset test`** - Test preset against current configuration
- **`preset delete`** - Remove presets with confirmation

### Smart Interactive Mode
- **`1mcp preset`** - Auto-detects existing presets and offers creation/editing options
- **TUI Interface** - Three-state checkbox selection (include/exclude/ignore)
- **Live Preview** - Real-time server matching as selections change
- **Strategy Selection** - OR/AND/Advanced filtering with clear explanations

### Advanced Filtering Capabilities
- **Simple comma-separated** - OR logic (`"web,api,database"`)
- **Boolean expressions** - Complex queries (`"(web OR api) AND database AND NOT experimental"`)
- **Multiple strategies** - Tag matching, OR logic, AND logic, Advanced JSON queries
- **Tag-based server filtering** - Seamless integration with existing tag system

### Dynamic URL Configuration
- **Query parameter switching** - `?preset=development` in URLs
- **Hot-reload support** - Real-time client notifications on preset changes
- **Persistent configuration** - Presets stored in `~/.config/1mcp/presets.json`
- **Automatic file watching** - Changes trigger immediate client updates

### Documentation & Integration
- **Comprehensive docs** - Full command documentation with examples
- **Multi-language support** - English and Chinese documentation
- **CLI help integration** - New `--config-dir` option for preset management
- **Backward compatibility** - Existing tag filtering methods still work

## Technical Implementation

### Architecture
- **Singleton managers** - Config and preset management with proper cleanup
- **Factory patterns** - Preset object creation and management
- **File system watching** - Hot-reload configuration changes
- **MCP protocol integration** - Real-time client notifications
- **TypeScript safety** - Strong typing throughout the codebase

### File Structure
```
src/preset/
├── types.ts          # Preset type definitions
├── manager.ts        # Preset management logic
├── commands/         # CLI command implementations
│   ├── create.ts     # Command-line preset creation
│   ├── edit.ts       # Interactive preset editing
│   ├── list.ts       # Preset listing
│   ├── show.ts       # Preset details
│   ├── url.ts        # URL generation
│   ├── test.ts       # Preset testing
│   └── delete.ts     # Preset deletion
└── index.ts          # Preset module exports
```

## Usage Examples

### Interactive Preset Creation
```bash
1mcp preset                    # Smart interactive mode
1mcp preset edit development  # Edit existing preset
```

### Command-Line Creation
```bash
1mcp preset create dev --filter "web,api,database"
1mcp preset create prod --filter "web AND database AND monitoring"
```

### Team Sharing
```bash
1mcp preset url team-dev       # Generate: http://localhost:3050/?preset=team-dev
```

## Breaking Changes
- None - fully backward compatible with existing configurations

## Testing Strategy
- Unit tests for preset management logic
- E2E tests for CLI commands
- Integration tests for file watching and hot-reload
- Manual testing documentation provided

Self-enumeration was failing when using GitHub tokens with `public_repo` scope instead of the full `repo` scope. The code was overly restrictive and only accepted the `repo` scope, even though `public_repo` scope provides sufficient permissions for enumerating public repositories and organizations.

## Changes Made

**Updated scope validation in `gatox/enumerate/enumerate.py`:**

1. **`self_enumeration()` method**: Modified scope check to accept both `repo` and `public_repo` scopes
2. **`validate_only()` method**: Updated to work with both scope types
3. **Error messages**: Updated to reflect the new supported scopes

**Before:**
```python
if "repo" not in self.user_perms["scopes"]:
    Output.error("Self-enumeration requires the repo scope!")
    return False
```

**After:**
```python
if "repo" not in self.user_perms["scopes"] and "public_repo" not in self.user_perms["scopes"]:
    Output.error("Self-enumeration requires the repo or public_repo scope!")
    return False
```

**Added comprehensive test coverage** to verify:
- Self-enumeration works with `public_repo` scope
- Self-enumeration still works with `repo` scope (backward compatibility)
- Proper failure when neither scope is present
- `validate_only` works with `public_repo` scope

## GitHub API Compatibility

This fix aligns with GitHub's permission model:
- `repo`: Full control of private repositories (includes public repo access)
- `public_repo`: Access to public repositories only

Both scopes provide the necessary permissions to call `/user/repos` and `/user/orgs` endpoints for public data enumeration.

The change is minimal and surgical, maintaining full backward compatibility while enabling the functionality with the more restrictive `public_repo` scope that many users prefer for security reasons.

Fixes #194.

## Summary

This PR implements comprehensive support for the `CREATE USER` statement in the ClickHouse SQL parser according to the [official ClickHouse documentation](https://clickhouse.com/docs/sql-reference/statements/create/user).

## Changes Made

### New Keywords Added
- `IDENTIFIED`, `GRANTEES`, `HOST`, `NAME`, `IP`, `KERBEROS`, `LDAP`, `REALM`, `SERVER`

### AST Structures Created
- **`CreateUser`** - Main CREATE USER AST node with support for all clauses
- **`AuthenticationClause`** - Handles authentication options (NOT IDENTIFIED, IDENTIFIED WITH various methods)
- **`HostClause`** - Handles host restrictions (LOCAL, NAME, REGEXP, IP, LIKE, ANY, NONE)
- **`DefaultRoleClause`** - Handles DEFAULT ROLE clause with multiple roles
- **`GranteesClause`** - Handles GRANTEES clause with EXCEPT support

### Parser Implementation
- **`parseCreateUser()`** - Main parser method for CREATE USER statements
- **`parseAuthenticationClause()`** - Parses authentication options
- **`parseHostClause()`** - Parses host restrictions  
- **`parseDefaultRoleClause()`** - Parses default roles
- **`parseGranteesClause()`** - Parses grantees with exception handling
- Updated DDL parser to recognize CREATE USER statements

## Supported Syntax

The implementation supports the full CREATE USER syntax as documented:

```sql
-- Basic usage
CREATE USER user1;
CREATE USER IF NOT EXISTS user2;
CREATE USER OR REPLACE user3;

-- Authentication methods
CREATE USER user4 NOT IDENTIFIED;
CREATE USER user5 IDENTIFIED WITH plaintext_password BY 'password';
CREATE USER user6 IDENTIFIED WITH sha256_password BY 'hash';
CREATE USER user7 IDENTIFIED WITH ldap SERVER 'ldap_server';
CREATE USER user8 IDENTIFIED WITH kerberos REALM 'EXAMPLE.COM';

-- Host restrictions
CREATE USER user9 HOST LOCAL;
CREATE USER user10 HOST NAME 'localhost';
CREATE USER user11 HOST REGEXP '.*\.example\.com';
CREATE USER user12 HOST IP '192.168.1.1';

-- Default roles and database
CREATE USER user13 DEFAULT ROLE role1, role2;
CREATE USER user14 DEFAULT DATABASE test_db;

-- Grantees with exceptions
CREATE USER user15 GRANTEES user1, user2 EXCEPT user3;

-- Settings
CREATE USER user16 SETTINGS max_memory_usage=5000000;

-- Complex multi-clause example
CREATE USER user17 
    IDENTIFIED WITH plaintext_password BY 'password'
    HOST NAME 'localhost'
    DEFAULT ROLE role1, role2
    DEFAULT DATABASE test_db
    GRANTEES user1, user2 EXCEPT user3
    SETTINGS max_memory_usage=5000000, readonly=1;
```

## Testing

- **32 comprehensive test cases** covering all syntax variations

This PR fixes an issue where the `enter` and `leave` methods in the `ASTVisitor` interface were unexported (lowercase), preventing external packages from overriding these methods when creating custom visitors.

## Problem

Users trying to implement custom visitors by embedding `DefaultASTVisitor` in external packages couldn't override the `enter` and `leave` methods:

```go
package client

import "github.com/AfterShip/clickhouse-sql-parser/parser"

type QueryVisitor struct {
    parser.DefaultASTVisitor
    stack []parser.Expr
}

// This would fail to compile - enter/leave methods are unexported
func (v *QueryVisitor) enter(expr parser.Expr) { /* ... */ }
func (v *QueryVisitor) leave(expr parser.Expr) { /* ... */ }
```

The only workaround was to define the custom visitor in the same package as `DefaultASTVisitor`.

## Solution

- Changed `enter(expr Expr)` to `Enter(expr Expr)` in the `ASTVisitor` interface
- Changed `leave(expr Expr)` to `Leave(expr Expr)` in the `ASTVisitor` interface
- Updated the `DefaultASTVisitor` implementation accordingly
- Updated all 326 calls to these methods throughout the AST node `Accept` methods
- Updated existing tests to use the new exported method names
- Added `TestVisitor_ExportedMethods` to verify external packages can override these methods

## Usage Example

Custom visitors can now be implemented in external packages:

```go
package client

import "github.com/AfterShip/clickhouse-sql-parser/parser"

type QueryVisitor struct {
    parser.DefaultASTVisitor
    stack []parser.Expr
}

func (v *QueryVisitor) Enter(expr parser.Expr) {
    v.stack = append(v.stack, expr)
}

func (v *QueryVisitor) Leave(expr parser.Expr) {
    if len(v.stack) > 0 {
        v.stack = v.stack[:len(v.stack)-1]
    }
}
```

## Breaking Changes

This is a breaking change for any code that currently overrides the unexported `enter`/`leave` methods within the same package. Such code should update to use the new `Enter`/`Leave` method names.

## Testing

- All existing tests pass (139 SQL test cases in the visitor test suite)
- Created external package test to verify the fix works
- Added regression test to ensure methods remain exported

Fixes #140.

Implements behavior changes to skip the initial greeting and start listening immediately when the ConversationalAgentService starts, while deferring memory extraction until after the first user utterance.

## Problem

Previously, when the ConversationalAgentService started, it would:
1. Speak a personalized greeting (e.g., "Hey [username]!")
2. Extract memories from the conversation history before any user input
3. Only then begin listening for user speech

This created an unnecessary delay and prevented users from speaking immediately upon service activation.

## Solution

The service now:
1. **Skips the greeting entirely** - No TTS output on startup
2. **Starts listening immediately** - STT pipeline begins right after service initialization
3. **Defers memory extraction** - Only triggers after the first user utterance is received

## Key Changes

### Service Startup Flow
```kotlin
// Before: Spoke greeting first
serviceScope.launch {
    if (conversationHistory.size == 1) {
        val greeting = getPersonalizedGreeting()
        speakAndThenListen(greeting)  // TTS then STT
    }
}

// After: Immediate listening
serviceScope.launch {
    Log.d("ConvAgent", "Starting immediate listening (no greeting)")
    startImmediateListening()  // Direct STT
}
```

### Memory Extraction Deferral
Added `hasHeardFirstUtterance` flag to track when the first user input is received:

```kotlin
if (!hasHeardFirstUtterance) {
    hasHeardFirstUtterance = true
    Log.d("ConvAgent", "First utterance received, triggering memory extraction")
    updateSystemPromptWithMemories()
}
```

### Robust Error Handling
- Graceful handling of memory extraction failures
- Proper permission error handling through existing STT error callbacks
- Comprehensive logging for debugging and monitoring

## Impact

- **Faster user interaction**: Users can speak immediately when the service starts
- **Better UX**: No forced waiting for greeting completion
- **Maintained functionality**: All existing features work the same after the first utterance
- **Cross-service compatibility**: All service callers (floating button, wake word, assist entry, main activity) benefit from immediate listening

## Testing

Added comprehensive unit tests covering:
- Flag initialization and state management
- Memory extraction timing and error handling
- Service startup behavior verification

The changes maintain backward compatibility with all existing permission handling and error recovery mechanisms.

The implementation uses a clean feature flag approach that:
- **Preserves all existing code** - no memory-related functionality was deleted
- **Enables easy restoration** - changing `MEMORY_ENABLED = true` will restore full functionality
- **Provides clear user communication** - users see consistent messaging that "Panda memory is turned off as of yet"
- **Maintains app stability** - conversational agent continues to work normally without memory features

## User Experience

Users will now see clear messaging throughout the app that memory functionality is temporarily disabled, while all other features (voice conversations, task execution, screen understanding) continue to work normally.

a.body:
This PR addresses the inefficient DataFrame concatenation pattern that was causing O(n²) performance degradation in the time series features extraction.

## Problem

In `timecopilot/agent.py`, the `tsfeatures_tool` function was concatenating DataFrames inside a loop:

```python
features_df: pd.DataFrame | None = None
for uid in ctx.deps.df["unique_id"].unique():
    features_df_uid = _get_feats(...)
    if features_df is None:
        features_df = features_df_uid
    else:
        features_df = pd.concat([features_df, features_df_uid])  # Inefficient!
```

This pattern causes pandas to allocate a new DataFrame with increasing size, copy all existing data, and then add the new chunk on each iteration. The total runtime grows quadratically with the number of unique IDs.

## Solution

Replaced with the efficient pattern that collects DataFrames in a list first, then concatenates once:

```python
features_dfs = []
for uid in ctx.deps.df["unique_id"].unique():
    features_df_uid = _get_feats(...)
    features_dfs.append(features_df_uid)
features_df = pd.concat(features_dfs) if features_dfs else pd.DataFrame()
```

## Changes

- **Performance**: Eliminated O(n²) complexity, now O(n)
- **Memory efficiency**: Reduced memory allocations and data copying
- **Robustness**: Added edge case handling for empty lists
- **Maintainability**: Cleaner, more readable code

## Testing

- Verified the new pattern produces identical results to the original
- Confirmed proper handling of edge cases (empty unique_id lists)
- Validated syntax correctness and no linting issues
- Checked entire codebase for similar patterns (none found)

The fix maintains full backward compatibility while significantly improving performance for datasets with many unique time series identifiers.

Fixes #104.

This PR implements a new security rule `Azure.ACR.ReplicaLocation` that validates container registry replica locations against allowed regions configuration.

## What's Changed

- **New Rule**: `Azure.ACR.ReplicaLocation` (AZR-000311)
  - Checks that all container registry replicas are deployed to allowed regions
  - Uses `AZURE_RESOURCE_ALLOWED_LOCATIONS` configuration (consistent with other location rules)
  - Categorized under Security baseline (SE:01)

## Implementation Details

The rule follows the established pattern from `Azure.Log.ReplicaLocation`:

```powershell
Rule 'Azure.ACR.ReplicaLocation' -Ref 'AZR-000311' -Type 'Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries' -If { IsExport } -Tag @{ release = 'GA'; ruleSet = '2025_06'; 'Azure.WAF/pillar' = 'Security'; } {
    $context = $PSRule.GetService('Azure.Context');
    $replications = @(GetSubResources -ResourceType 'Microsoft.ContainerRegistry/registries/replications');
    
    if ($replications.Length -eq 0) {
        return $Assert.Pass();
    }

    foreach ($replica in $replications) {
        $location = $replica.Location;
        $Assert.Create('Location', [bool]$context.IsAllowedLocation($location), $LocalizedData.LocationNotAllowed, @($location));
    }
}
```

## Test Coverage

- Added test registry with replica in disallowed region (`registry-K` with `region3`)
- Validates pass/fail scenarios with configuration: `['region', 'region2']`
- Ensures registries without replicas pass the rule

## Configuration Example

```yaml
configuration:
  AZURE_RESOURCE_ALLOWED_LOCATIONS:
  - australiaeast
  - australiasoutheast
```

## Documentation

- Created comprehensive rule documentation with ARM/Bicep examples
- Updated module documentation in Security baseline section
- Added to both English and Spanish documentation

This addresses organizations' data residency requirements by ensuring container registry replicas are only deployed to approved regions.

Fixes #3442.

The rule validates that:

This PR adds version constraints to the Dependabot configuration to ensure Kubernetes dependencies remain compatible with versions 1.30, 1.31, and 1.32.

## Problem
Without version constraints, Dependabot could automatically update Kubernetes dependencies to v0.33.x or higher, which would correspond to Kubernetes 1.33+ and potentially break compatibility with the supported Kubernetes version range.

## Solution
Added `ignore` constraints to all `gomod` package ecosystem entries in `.github/dependabot.yaml` to prevent updates beyond the compatibility range:

### Kubernetes Dependencies Constrained:
- `k8s.io/api` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0
- `k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0  
- `k8s.io/apimachinery` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0
- `k8s.io/client-go` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0
- `k8s.io/kubelet` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0
- `k8s.io/kubectl` - ignore versions >= v0.33.0

### Directories Updated:
- Main repository root (`/`)
- Azure IPAM directory (`/azure-ipam`)
- Build tools directory (`/build/tools`)
- Azure NPM to Cilium validator (`/tools/azure-npm-to-cilium-validator`) - newly added entry
- Release/v1.5 branch entries (both root and azure-ipam)
- Release/v1.4 branch entries (both root and azure-ipam)

### Version Mapping:
- v0.30.x = Kubernetes 1.30.x ✅ (allowed)
- v0.31.x = Kubernetes 1.31.x ✅ (allowed) 
- v0.32.x = Kubernetes 1.32.x ✅ (allowed)
- v0.33.x = Kubernetes 1.33.x ❌ (ignored)

## Testing
- ✅ YAML syntax validated
- ✅ Build successful with no functional changes
- ✅ All directories containing k8s.io dependencies are covered

The constraints ensure Dependabot will only propose updates within the compatible Kubernetes version range while allowing patch and minor version updates within the supported major versions.

Fixes #3726.

The `func pack` command was failing for C# in-process projects with the error "Pack command doesn't work for dotnet functions", while the same projects worked fine with `func azure functionapp publish`. This inconsistency made it impossible to create deployment packages manually for C# in-process projects.

I've also added E2E tests that test the basic functionality for `func pack` for the other worker runtimes.

## Root Cause
The issue was in `PackAction.cs` where the call to `ZipHelper.GetAppZipFile()` was missing the `ignoreDotNetCheck: true` parameter. This caused the following condition in `ZipHelper.cs` to evaluate to `true` and throw an exception:

```csharp
if (GlobalCoreToolsSettings.CurrentWorkerRuntime == WorkerRuntime.Dotnet && 
    !ignoreDotNetCheck && !noBuild && buildOption != BuildOption.Remote)
{
    throw new CliException("Pack command doesn't work for dotnet functions");
}
```

## Solution
Updated `PackAction.cs` to pass `ignoreDotNetCheck: true` to match the pattern used in `PublishFunctionAppAction.cs`:

**Before:**
```csharp
var stream = await ZipHelper.GetAppZipFile(functionAppRoot, BuildNativeDeps, 
    noBuild: false, buildOption: BuildOption.Default, additionalPackages: AdditionalPackages);
```

**After:**
```csharp
var stream = await ZipHelper.GetAppZipFile(functionAppRoot, BuildNativeDeps, BuildOption.Default, 
    noBuild: false, ignoreParser: null, AdditionalPackages, ignoreDotNetCheck: true);
```

## Testing
- Added unit test `PackActionTests.cs` to verify the exception is no longer thrown
- Added E2E test `DotnetInProcessPackTests.cs` for full workflow validation
- Verified the fix follows the same pattern as the working publish functionality

This change allows C# in-process projects to use `func pack` successfully, matching the behavior already available for C# isolated projects and the publish command.

Fixes #3623.

## Summary

This PR implements automatic remote build detection for the `func pack` command when running Python function apps on Windows machines that target Linux environments. This addresses the cross-platform scenario where Python dependencies need to be built for the correct target platform.

## Problem

Previously, the `func pack` command always used local builds regardless of the development platform, which could cause issues when:
- Developing Python function apps on Windows 
- The function app targets Linux (typical for Azure Functions Python runtime)
- Dependencies in `requirements.txt` contain native code that needs to be compiled for Linux

This resulted in Windows-compiled dependencies being packaged, which would fail when deployed to Linux-based Azure Functions.

## Solution

Extended the existing remote build detection logic from the `func azure functionapp publish` command to the `func pack` command:

### Changes Made

1. **PackAction.cs**: Modified to automatically resolve build options instead of using hardcoded `BuildOption.Default`
   ```csharp
   // Before
   var stream = await ZipHelper.GetAppZipFile(functionAppRoot, BuildNativeDeps, noBuild: false, buildOption: BuildOption.Default, additionalPackages: AdditionalPackages);
   
   // After  
   var buildOption = PublishHelper.ResolveBuildOption(BuildOption.Default, workerRuntime, site: null, BuildNativeDeps, noBuild: false);
   var stream = await ZipHelper.GetAppZipFile(functionAppRoot, BuildNativeDeps, noBuild: false, buildOption: buildOption, additionalPackages: AdditionalPackages);
   ```

### Behavior

The `func pack` command will now automatically use remote build when:
- ✅ Worker runtime is Python
- ✅ `requirements.txt` exists and has content  

All other scenarios maintain existing behavior:
- ❌ Non-Python runtimes → Default build
- ❌ No `requirements.txt` → Default build  
- ❌ Empty `requirements.txt` → Default build
- ❌ Explicit `--build-native-deps` flags → Respect user choice

### Testing

Added comprehensive unit tests covering:
- Python apps with/without `requirements.txt`
- Different worker runtimes (Python, Node.js, etc.)
- Build option precedence and edge cases
- File system scenarios with temporary test directories

## Benefits

- **Seamless cross-platform development**: Python developers on Windows get correct Linux-compatible packages automatically
- **No breaking changes**: Existing behavior maintained for all other scenarios
- **Consistent with publish command**: Uses same logic as `func azure functionapp publish`
- **No additional flags required**: Works automatically based on project detection

Fixes #4255.

Fixes the user prompt order for Python Cosmos DB trigger templates to follow Azure resource hierarchy, resolving microsoft/vscode-azurefunctions#4672.

## Problem

The Python Cosmos DB trigger template (V2) was prompting users in an illogical order that goes against typical user mental models and Azure portal navigation patterns:

1. **Container name** (specific detail)
2. **Database name** (child context)  
3. **Database account** (top-level context)

This forced users to know specific container and database names before selecting the broader database account context.

## Solution

Reordered the user prompts to follow the logical Azure resource hierarchy:

1. **Database account/connection** (top-level resource selection)
2. **Database name** (child of account)
3. **Container name** (child of database)

Updated `Functions.Templates/Templates-v2/CosmosDbTrigger-Python/template.json` to reorder the `inputs` array in all 4 job configurations:

**Before:**
```json
"inputs": [
  {"paramId": "cosmosDbTrigger-containerName"},
  {"paramId": "cosmosDbTrigger-databaseName"},  
  {"paramId": "cosmosDbTrigger-connection"}
]
```

**After:**
```json
"inputs": [
  {"paramId": "cosmosDbTrigger-connection"},
  {"paramId": "cosmosDbTrigger-databaseName"},
  {"paramId": "cosmosDbTrigger-containerName"}
]
```

## Impact

This change improves the developer experience by aligning the prompt order with:
- Azure portal resource hierarchy (Account → Database → Container)
- Natural user mental models
- Industry standard navigation patterns

The fix is backward compatible and only affects the order of prompts, not functionality.

### Key Changes

1. **Created LCL file processor** (`Build/gulp-utils/gulp-lcl-js/index.js`)
   - Parses LCX schema XML files using xmldom
   - Extracts translated strings from `<Tgt>` elements within `<Item>` nodes
   - Converts translations to JSON format
   - Filters out structural elements to include only actual translation keys

2. **Updated build tasks** (`Build/gulpfile.js`)
   - Modified `resources-convert` task to process both existing `.resx` files and new `.lcl` files
   - Added support for the `Resources_lcl` directory structure
   - Maintains backward compatibility with existing resource processing

3. **Removed deprecated cs-CZ directory**
   - Deleted `Functions.Templates/Resources/cs-CZ` as it's superseded by the Resources_lcl approach

4. **Added required dependency**

### Output Format

**Resources.json** and **Resources.en-US.json**:

{

## Problem

Users installing Azure MCP Server on Ubuntu reported cryptic errors when platform-specific packages fail to install:

```
Failed to load platform specific package '@azure/mcp-linux-x64': Cannot find module '@azure/mcp-linux-x64'
```

This error provided no actionable guidance for users to resolve the issue, leading to support requests and failed installations.

## Root Cause

The wrapper package correctly attempts to load platform-specific packages (e.g., `@azure/mcp-linux-x64` for Linux x64), but when these packages are missing due to:
- Network connectivity issues during installation
- npm cache corruption
- Incomplete downloads
- Corporate firewall/proxy restrictions

...the error handling was inadequate and didn't help users troubleshoot.

## Solution

### Enhanced Error Handling
Improved the wrapper's error handling to provide clear, actionable troubleshooting steps:

```bash
❌ Failed to load platform specific package '@azure/mcp-linux-x64'

🔍 Troubleshooting steps:

1. Clear npm cache and reinstall:
   npm cache clean --force
   npm uninstall -g @azure/mcp
   npm install -g @azure/mcp@latest

2. If using npx, clear the cache:
   npx clear-npx-cache
   npx -y @azure/mcp@latest server start

3. Manually install the platform package:
   npm install @azure/mcp-linux-x64@latest

4. Check your internet connection and try again

5. If the issue persists, please report it at:
   https://github.com/Azure/azure-mcp/issues
```

### Enhanced Documentation
Added a comprehensive troubleshooting section to `TROUBLESHOOTING.md` covering:
- Common causes of platform package installation failures
- Step-by-step resolution instructions

- Platform-specific installation commands

This PR removes 4 unnecessary Maven plugins from the azure-openrewrite pom.xml that are not required for the basic build process. Each plugin was systematically tested by removing it and running `mvn clean install` to verify the build still succeeds.

## Plugins Removed (Unnecessary)
- **maven-pmd-plugin**: Only used for PMD reports via `mvn pmd:pmd`, not required for build
- **maven-checkstyle-plugin**: Code quality plugin not required for build success  
- **spotbugs-maven-plugin**: Static analysis tool not required for build success
- **spotless-maven-plugin**: Was already skipped with `<skip>true</skip>` configuration

## Plugins Kept (Essential)
- **maven-source-plugin**: Required for generating sources JAR needed for Maven Central publishing
- **maven-antrun-plugin**: Required for copying POM file to target directory for proper artifact publishing
- **maven-javadoc-plugin**: Required for generating javadoc JAR needed for Maven Central publishing
- **codesnippet-maven-plugin**: Required for updating and verifying code snippets in documentation

## Testing Methodology
Each plugin was individually removed and tested with `mvn clean install` to verify:
1. Build compilation succeeds
2. Test compilation succeeds  
3. JAR packaging succeeds
4. Required artifacts are generated

For plugins determined to be necessary, the specific build failure or missing artifact was documented to justify keeping them.

## Impact
- Reduces POM complexity by removing 75 lines of unused plugin configuration
- Improves build performance by eliminating unnecessary plugin executions
- Maintains all essential functionality for artifact generation and publishing

Build verification: ✅ `mvn clean install` passes after plugin removal

Fixes #45594.

This PR deprecates the `SharedTokenCacheCredential` and `SharedTokenCacheCredentialBuilder` classes and removes `SharedTokenCacheCredential` from the `DefaultAzureCredential` authentication chain.

## Background

`SharedTokenCacheCredential` was originally introduced in September 2019 to enable interoperability with Visual Studio, which was the only application that wrote to the shared token cache. Since Visual Studio was the sole consumer of this credential type, and there are now better alternatives for local development authentication, this credential has been deprecated.

## Changes Made

### Deprecation
- Added `@Deprecated` annotation to `SharedTokenCacheCredential` class with clear deprecation message
- Added `@Deprecated` annotation to `SharedTokenCacheCredentialBuilder` class with clear deprecation message
- Deprecation messages direct users to use other developer credentials like `AzureCliCredential`, `AzureDeveloperCliCredential`, `AzurePowerShellCredential`, or `IntelliJCredential`

### DefaultAzureCredential Updates
- Removed `SharedTokenCacheCredential` from the credential chain in `DefaultAzureCredentialBuilder.getCredentialsChain()`
- Updated `DefaultAzureCredential` JavaDoc to remove reference to `SharedTokenCacheCredential`
- Adjusted ArrayList initial capacity from 8 to 7 to match the new credential count

### Test Updates
- Updated `testDeveloperOnlyCredentialsChain` to expect 4 developer credentials instead of 5
- Updated `testDefaultCredentialChainWithoutFilter` to expect 7 total credentials instead of 8
- Updated `testNoCredentialWorks` to remove `SharedTokenCacheCredential` mock construction
- All credential order assertions updated to reflect the new chain structure

## Authentication Chain Impact

**Before:**
1. EnvironmentCredential
2. WorkloadIdentityCredential  
3. ManagedIdentityCredential
4. SharedTokenCacheCredential ← **Removed**
5. IntelliJCredential
6. AzureCliCredential
7. AzurePowerShellCredential
8. AzureDeveloperCliCredential

**After:**
1. EnvironmentCredential
2. WorkloadIdentityCredential
3. ManagedIdentityCredential
4. IntelliJCredential
5. AzureCliCredential
6. AzurePowerShellCredential
7. AzureDeveloperCliCredential

## Backward Compatibility

The deprecated classes remain available for direct instantiation and use, ensuring existing code continues to work. However, users are encouraged to migrate to the recommended alternatives for local development scenarios.

Fixes #45762.

This PR fixes the Node.js DEP0190 deprecation warning that occurs when using `AzureCliCredential` with Node.js v24+.

## Issue
The `getAzureCliAccessToken` method was calling `child_process.execFile` with `shell: true`, which triggers Node.js deprecation warning DEP0190:

```
(node:1252) [DEP0190] DeprecationWarning: Passing args to a child process with shell option true can lead to security vulnerabilities, as the arguments are not escaped, only concatenated.
```

## Solution
Removed the `shell: true` option from the `execFile` call. This approach:

1. **Eliminates the deprecation warning** - `execFile` without shell is the recommended secure approach
2. **Maintains functionality** - All existing behavior is preserved as verified by comprehensive test suite
3. **Improves security** - Avoids potential argument injection vulnerabilities
4. **Aligns with existing patterns** - `AzureDeveloperCliCredential` already uses this approach successfully

## Changes
- **Source**: Removed `shell: true` from `execFile` options in `azureCliCredential.ts`
- **Tests**: Updated test expectations to check for `shell: undefined` instead of `shell: true`
- **Impact**: Minimal change (1 line in source, 16 lines in tests)

## Verification
- ✅ All existing tests pass
- ✅ Build succeeds
- ✅ Linting passes
- ✅ No functional changes to credential behavior

Fixes #34876.

## Summary

This PR implements handling for HTTP 410 (Gone) status responses in the ManagedIdentityCredential retry policy to meet Azure IMDS service requirements for at least 70 seconds total retry duration.

## Problem

The current `imdsRetryPolicy` only retries on 404 status codes, but according to [Azure IMDS documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/virtual-machines/instance-metadata-service?tabs=windows#errors-and-debugging), 410 status codes can also be returned when the identity is still being set up and require special handling with sufficient retry duration.

## Solution

Following the .NET SDK implementation approach, this PR:

1. **Adds 410 status code to retry logic** alongside existing 404 handling
2. **Enforces minimum 3-second initial delay** for 410 responses to ensure at least 70 seconds total retry duration
3. **Preserves existing behavior** for 404 responses and all other scenarios

### Technical Implementation

```typescript
// For 410 responses, use minimum 3-second delay to ensure at least 70 seconds total retry duration
const initialDelayMs = response?.status === 410 
  ? Math.max(MIN_DELAY_FOR_410_MS, msiRetryConfig.startDelayInMs)
  : msiRetryConfig.startDelayInMs;
```

The 3-second minimum is calculated based on exponential backoff with 5 retries:
- Delays: d, 2d, 4d, 8d, 16d = 31d total
- With jitter (80% minimum): 31d × 0.8 ≥ 70 seconds
- Therefore: d ≥ 2.82 seconds, using 3 seconds for safety

## Validation

✅ **410 responses**: Retry with 3-second minimum delay, achieving 70+ second total duration  
✅ **404 responses**: Continue using configured delay (unchanged behavior)  
✅ **Other status codes**: No retries (unchanged behavior)  
✅ **Larger configured delays**: Preserved when > 3 seconds for 410 responses  
✅ **All tests pass**: Comprehensive test coverage added

Example test output showing the 70-second requirement is met:
```
Testing total retry duration for 410 responses...
Total scheduled delay: 70114ms (70.1s)
Requirement met: YES
```

## Changes Made

- **Updated `imdsRetryPolicy.ts`**: Added 410 status handling with minimum delay logic
- **Enhanced documentation**: Updated JSDoc comments to reflect new behavior  
- **Added comprehensive tests**: Covers 410 handling, delay enforcement, and regression prevention

## Backward Compatibility

Zero breaking changes - all existing behavior is preserved for 404 responses and other status codes.

Fixes #34961.

This PR deprecates the `UseEmbeddedWebView` property in the `BrowserCustomizationOptions` class by adding the `[Obsolete]` attribute with an appropriate deprecation message.

## Changes Made

- Added `[Obsolete]` attribute to the `UseEmbeddedWebView` property with the message: "This option requires additional dependencies on Microsoft.Identity.Client.Desktop and is no longer supported. Consider using brokered authentication instead"
- Updated API surface files for both .NET 8.0 and .NET Standard 2.0 to reflect the deprecation
- Added `#pragma warning disable CS0618` suppressions in:
  - Test methods that verify the property functionality 
  - Internal implementation code in `MsalPublicClient.cs` that still needs to support the property for backward compatibility
- Added changelog entry documenting the deprecation in the 1.17.0-beta.1 (Unreleased) section

## Background

The embedded browser functionality depends on Windows Forms, which requires the Microsoft.Identity.Client.Desktop assembly. Azure.Identity does not support the `WithWindowsEmbeddedBrowserSupport` scenario offered by MSAL directly, so users would need to use MSAL directly to utilize this feature. To address this limitation, we are deprecating this property and recommending users consider brokered authentication instead.

## Backward Compatibility

The property remains functional for existing code but will now emit compiler warnings encouraging migration to alternative authentication methods. All existing tests continue to pass with appropriate warning suppressions.

Fixes #50495.

This PR implements a new static analysis rule `AZC0034` for the Azure.ClientSdk.Analyzers to detect duplicate type names that could conflict with .NET platform types or violate Azure SDK naming conventions.

## What this analyzer detects

**Platform type conflicts**: Flags public types in Azure namespaces that have the same name as common .NET types:
```csharp
namespace Azure.Storage
{
    public class String { } // ❌ AZC0034: Conflicts with System.String
    public class Task { }   // ❌ AZC0034: Conflicts with System.Threading.Tasks.Task
    public class List { }   // ❌ AZC0034: Conflicts with System.Collections.Generic.List<T>
}
```

**Misused nested-only types**: Ensures that certain type names are only used as nested types:
```csharp
namespace Azure.Storage
{
    // ❌ AZC0034: ServiceVersion should only be used as nested type
    public enum ServiceVersion { V2020_02_10 }
    
    public class BlobClient
    {
        // ✅ Allowed: ServiceVersion properly nested
        public enum ServiceVersion { V2020_02_10, V2021_04_10 }
    }
}
```

## Key features

- **30+ platform types detected**: Covers common System types, collections, exceptions, async types, interfaces, and attributes
- **Smart nesting rules**: Allows `ServiceVersion` and `Enumerator` when properly nested, flags them at top level
- **Azure-scoped**: Only analyzes public types in namespaces starting with "Azure"
- **Performance optimized**: Early returns for non-public types and non-Azure namespaces

## Test coverage

Added 14 comprehensive test cases covering:
- Platform type conflicts (String, List, Dictionary, Task, Exception types)
- Interface conflicts (IDisposable, IComparable)
- Proper nesting behavior for ServiceVersion and Enumerator
- Non-public type exclusions
- Non-Azure namespace exclusions
- Multiple nesting levels and protected nested types

All existing tests continue to pass (316 total tests, zero build warnings).

This addresses the requirement to ensure Azure SDK types don't conflict with .NET platform types while allowing standard nested type patterns used across Azure SDK libraries.

Fixes #10841.

- Updated `tests/e2e/max/main.test.bicep` with multiple configuration examples including `aad_auth_only` and `innodb_buffer_pool_size`

Before this change, users needed separate resources:
```bicep
module mysqlServer 'br/public:avm/res/db-for-my-sql/flexible-server:<version>' = {
  params: {
    name: 'my-server'
    // ... other params
  }

        value: 'ON'
      }
    ]
  }
}

- Follows the same pattern established by the PostgreSQL flexible server module
- Uses resource type `Microsoft.DBforMySQL/flexibleServers/configurations@2024-10-01-preview`
- Maintains backward compatibility - existing deployments continue to work unchanged

a.body:
## Problem

When using MSAL Angular standalone components, users experience infinite redirect loops after authentication when the URL contains encoded apostrophes (`%27`) in query parameters. For example:

```
https://localhost:4200/profile?comments=blah%27blah
```

After authentication, the app gets stuck in a redirect loop instead of displaying the intended page.

## Root Cause

The issue occurs in `RedirectClient.handleRedirectPromise()` during URL comparison. The method compares the stored login request URL with the current URL to determine if navigation is needed. However, the comparison doesn't handle URL encoding consistently:

- **Stored URL**: `https://localhost:4200/profile?comments=blah%27blah` (encoded apostrophe)
- **Current URL**: `https://localhost:4200/profile?comments=blah'blah` (decoded apostrophe)

Since `%27` ≠ `'` after normalization, MSAL thinks it's not on the correct page and attempts to navigate back, causing an infinite loop.

## Solution

Added a new `normalizeUrlForComparison()` method in `RedirectClient` that:

1. Uses the native `URL` constructor to handle encoding consistently
2. Ensures both URLs are normalized to the same encoding format
3. Preserves existing canonicalization logic
4. Includes graceful error handling with fallback

```typescript
private normalizeUrlForComparison(url: string): string {
    if (!url) return url;
    
    const urlWithoutHash = url.split("#")[0];
    try {
        const urlObj = new URL(urlWithoutHash);
        const normalizedUrl = urlObj.origin + urlObj.pathname + urlObj.search;
        return UrlString.canonicalizeUri(normalizedUrl);
    } catch (e) {
        // Fallback to original logic
        return UrlString.canonicalizeUri(urlWithoutHash);
    }
}
```

## Testing

Added comprehensive test case covering:
- ✅ Encoded vs decoded apostrophe scenario (the original issue)
- ✅ Multiple encoded characters
- ✅ Hash handling in redirect scenarios
- ✅ Edge cases and error conditions

## Impact

- **Fixes redirect loops** for URLs with encoded special characters
- **Zero breaking changes** - maintains backward compatibility
- **Minimal performance impact** - only affects URL comparison logic
- **Robust solution** - handles all URL-encoded characters consistently

## Before/After

**Before (broken):**
```
Stored:  https://localhost:4200/profile?comments=blah%27blah
Current: https://localhost:4200/profile?comments=blah'blah
Match: false → Redirect loop
```

**After (fixed):**
```  
Stored:  https://localhost:4200/profile?comments=blah%27blah
Current: https://localhost:4200/profile?comments=blah'blah  
Match: true → Normal flow continues
```

Fixes #7636.

## Problem

The `OidcIdpSignedAssertionLoader` class required `IConfiguration` to be explicitly registered in the service collection, causing a `System.InvalidOperationException` when trying to resolve `ICustomSignedAssertionProvider` implementations:

```csharp
// This would fail without explicit IConfiguration registration
var oidcIdpSignedAssertionLoader = serviceProvider.GetService<IOidcIdpSignedAssertionLoader>();
```

Error message:
```
System.InvalidOperationException : Unable to resolve service for type 'Microsoft.Extensions.Configuration.IConfiguration' while attempting to activate 'Microsoft.Identity.Web.OidcFic.OidcIdpSignedAssertionLoader'.
```

## Solution

Following the design proposal from @jmprieur, this PR implements:

1. **Constructor Change**: Modified `OidcIdpSignedAssertionLoader` constructor to accept `IServiceProvider` instead of `IConfiguration`
2. **Just-in-Time Resolution**: Added code to resolve `IConfiguration` from service provider only when needed
3. **Conditional Usage**: Configuration binding only occurs when both conditions are met:
   - `microsoftIdentityApplicationOptions.Instance` is null or empty
   - `microsoftIdentityApplicationOptions.Authority` equals "//v2.0"
4. **Error Handling**: Meaningful error message with troubleshooting link when `IConfiguration` is needed but not available
5. **Performance Logging**: Added debug logging for configuration binding operations

## Changes Made

### Before
```csharp
public OidcIdpSignedAssertionLoader(ILogger<OidcIdpSignedAssertionLoader> logger,

```

### After
```csharp
public OidcIdpSignedAssertionLoader(ILogger<OidcIdpSignedAssertionLoader> logger,
    IOptionsMonitor<MicrosoftIdentityApplicationOptions> options,
    IServiceProvider serviceProvider,  // Service locator for just-in-time resolution
    ITokenAcquirerFactory tokenAcquirerFactory)
```

- ✅ **Resolves the original issue** - service can be resolved without explicit `IConfiguration` registration
- ✅ **Maintains backward compatibility** - existing code continues to work
- ✅ **Provides clear error messages** when configuration is actually needed but not available
- ✅ **Follows dependency injection best practices** with service locator pattern only when necessary
- ✅ **Includes high performance logging** as requested in the design proposal

- New scenarios where `IConfiguration` is not registered will work unless configuration binding is specifically needed

## Summary Fixes #207 by removing the legacy interactive prompting feature that was causing the tool to crash when run without proper configuration. The tool now provides clear, actionable error messages instead of prompting users for partial configuration. ## Problem The Data Migration Tool had legacy interactive behavior that would: 1. Prompt users to select source/sink from a numbered list if not specified 2. Prompt for settings file path if not found 3. Crash with an exception after prompting because other required settings were missing This created a confusing user experience as shown in the issue - users would select "15 SqlServer" as source and "3 Cosmos-nosql" as sink, only to have the tool crash because connection strings and other required settings weren't configured. ## Solution Removed all interactive prompting and added proper validation that fails fast with helpful error messages: ### When `migrationsettings.json` is missing: ``` Error: Settings file 'migrationsettings.json' not found. Please provide a valid settings file or specify --source and --sink options. Use --help for more information. ``` ### When Source/Sink are not configured: ``` Error: Invalid configuration. Both Source and Sink must be specified. The settings file 'migrationsettings.json' is missing required Source or Sink values. Please provide valid Source and Sink in the settings file or via command line arguments. Use --help for more information. ``` ### When extension name is invalid: ``` Source extension 'invalid-name' not found. Use 'dmt list' to see available extensions. ``` ## Changes - **RunCommand.cs**: - Added validation in `InvokeAsync` to check for missing settings file and incomplete configuration - Removed interactive prompting loop from `GetExtensionSelection` - Removed settings file path prompting from `BuildSettingsConfiguration` - All methods now throw clear exceptions or return error codes with helpful messages - **RunCommandTests.cs**: Added 5 new test cases to validate the new behavior ## Testing - ✅ All existing tests continue to pass (no breaking changes to valid configurations) - ✅ 5 new test cases validate error handling for invalid configurations - ✅ Manual testing verified all error scenarios display helpful messages - ✅ Tool works correctly when proper configuration is provided via settings file or command-line arguments ## Benefits 1. **Clearer UX**: Users get immediate, actionable feedback instead of being prompted for incomplete configuration 2. **Better error messages**: Guidance to use `--help` and `dmt list` commands 3. **Fail fast**: Tool exits with error code 1 and clear message instead of prompting and crashing 4. **Consistent with modern CLI tools**: No interactive prompts, all configuration via files or arguments ## Breaking Changes This removes the interactive prompting behavior. Users who relied on being prompted to select source/sink will need to specify them via: - Command-line: `dmt --source json --sink cosmos-nosql ...` - Settings file: Properly configured `migrationsettings.json` However, the old interactive behavior would crash anyway after prompting, so this change improves the user experience for all scenarios.

We should no longer prompt the user and instead if the tool is run without arguments and the migrationsettings.json in the current directory is invalid we should indicate to the user it's invalid and then display the help information. If no migrationsettings.json is present the help should be displayed. If arguments are incorrect, we should indicate invalid argument and display the help > > ## Comments on the Issue (you are @copilot in this section) > > > @philnach > @markjbrown / @bowencode , dmt asks the user to select a sink and source if not present in the migrationsettings.json, but dmt fails with an exception since it doesn't ask for the missed settings. Is there a scenario where it would work? > > Example: > > > > @markjbrown > Something wrong about this issue. That's not how it works, and it is not documented to work that way. > > @LeonSweden Users are supposed to fill in the migrationsettings.json before they run the tool. Are you using the old desktop GUI tool? If so, this retired and no longer supported. > > > @philnach > @markjbrown, if you just run DMT with the default settings file. you'll see the above behavior. We should just print out the command line help and not provide any settings. This PR reworks the `CONTRIBUTING.md` and `formatting.md` files to make them accessible for first-time, non-developer users who have never used GitHub or git before, and fixes formatting inconsistencies across all chapter files.

## Key Changes

### CONTRIBUTING.md Improvements

- **Simplified for beginners**: Completely rewritten with friendly, conversational language that assumes no prior GitHub knowledge
- **Clearer step-by-step guide**: Detailed walkthrough of the contribution process with simple explanations (e.g., "fork" is explained as "your own copy of the project")
- **Removed technical sections**: Removed the "Editing Chapter Pages" section to focus on content contributions that are appropriate for non-technical users
- **Better organization**: Changed "Index" to "What's Inside This Guide" and restructured sections for easier navigation
- **Encouraging tone**: Added welcoming messages and emojis to make the guide feel approachable (🎉💜)
- **Simplified warnings**: Clear, plain-language notes about not editing auto-generated HTML files
- **Fixed typos and grammar**: Corrected "brach" → "branch", "upto date" → "up to date", and other improvements

### formatting.md Improvements

- **Beginner-friendly structure**: Each tag now has "What it does", "When to use it", and "How to use it" sections for clarity
- **Plain language throughout**: Replaced technical terminology with simple explanations (e.g., "horizontal rulers" → "horizontal line to separate sections")
- **Better organization**: Changed "General Rules" to "Basic Rules" and "Supported Tags" to "How to Use Tags" for a more approachable feel
- **Quick reference table**: Renamed "Summary of Tags" to "Quick Reference Table" with friendlier column headers ("What It's For" instead of "Purpose")
- **Practical tips**: Added "Quick Tips" section with helpful advice in plain English
- **Cross-referenced documentation**: Added TIP callout linking to the How to Contribute guide

### Chapter Files Formatting Fixes

Fixed formatting inconsistencies across all chapter files in the `/chapters` directory:

- **Bracket consistency**: Ensured `<@>` and `<!>` tags generally use `[..]` brackets, while preserving special characters like `「..」` and `『..』` for proper nouns, special terms, and skill names within system messages
- **Quote brackets**: Ensured `<&>` tags use `「..」` brackets for quote formatting
- **Fixed mismatched brackets**: Corrected unclosed tags and bracket mismatches
- **Removed trailing whitespace**: Cleaned up 255+ instances of trailing whitespace
- **Replaced tabs with spaces**: Converted tab characters to spaces for consistency
- **Standardized box unicode**: Replaced all box character variants (◻️◼️⬛⬜◻◼) with the standard ■ character for redacted/censored content (582 replacements across 46 files)
- **Fixed outer god dialogue formatting**: Ensured `<#>` tags use proper 【】 brackets for outer god speech. Only dialogues explicitly containing 【】 brackets are tagged as `<#>` outer god speech, as ■ (censored blocks) can appear in multiple types of messages and are not reliable indicators of outer god dialogue
- **All files validated**: All 938 chapter files now follow consistent formatting standards

## Impact

These changes make the documentation accessible to first-time contributors with no technical background. The guides now use simple, friendly language and provide clear explanations that assume no prior knowledge of GitHub, git, or web development. Additionally, all chapter files now have consistent formatting with proper bracket usage, correct dialogue tag assignments (using 【】 brackets as the definitive marker for outer god speech), and standardized characters, making the content cleaner and easier to maintain. This should significantly lower the barrier to entry for community contributions.

## Critical Database Compatibility Fix

**Realm Database**: `12.6.2` → `20.1.0`

Fixed the critical Android crash issue that occurs when using Realm with React Native 0.80+. The crash was caused by React Native 0.80's updated JSI implementation requiring newer Realm versions. - Updated Gradle autolinking configuration for React Native 0.80.2

## Problem

The iOS app was crashing with the following error:

```
Exception thrown while executing UI block: -[RCTView setSheetLargestUndimmedDetent:]: 
unrecognized selector sent to instance
```

This error occurred because the project was using an outdated AppDelegate pattern that doesn't properly support React Native's new architecture (Fabric/TurboModules), which is enabled in this project (`RCTNewArchEnabled = true` in Info.plist).

## Root Cause

The legacy AppDelegate implementation manually created and managed the RCTBridge and RCTRootView, which doesn't properly handle the new React Native architecture's view initialization and lifecycle management. This leads to iOS APIs like `setSheetLargestUndimmedDetent` being called on views that aren't properly initialized with the new architecture.

## Solution

Upgraded the AppDelegate to use React Native 0.80's modern template pattern:

### Before (Legacy Pattern):
```objc
@interface AppDelegate : UIResponder <UIApplicationDelegate, RCTBridgeDelegate>
@property (nonatomic, strong) UIWindow *window;

// Manual bridge and root view creation
RCTBridge *bridge = [[RCTBridge alloc] initWithDelegate:self launchOptions:launchOptions];
RCTRootView *rootView = [[RCTRootView alloc] initWithBridge:bridge...];
// Manual window setup...
```

### After (Modern Template):
```objc
@interface AppDelegate : RCTAppDelegate

// Simplified initialization
self.moduleName = @"GSYGithubApp";
self.initialProps = @{};
return [super application:application didFinishLaunchingWithOptions:launchOptions];
```

## Key Changes

1. **AppDelegate.h**: Changed inheritance from `UIResponder <UIApplicationDelegate, RCTBridgeDelegate>` to `RCTAppDelegate`
2. **AppDelegate.m**: Replaced manual bridge/root view setup with modern pattern that delegates to `RCTAppDelegate`
3. **Proper Architecture Support**: The new pattern properly handles both old and new React Native architectures
4. **Bundle Loading**: Added proper `bundleURL` method for consistent bundle loading

## Expected Result

The iOS app now properly initializes with React Native's new architecture, resolving the `setSheetLargestUndimmedDetent` selector error and ensuring compatibility with modern iOS APIs while maintaining all existing functionality.

This change follows React Native's official migration path and ensures the app works correctly with the new architecture features already enabled in the project.

## Overview
Fixes two critical bugs in the calendar management functionality where calendars could not be deleted and access token operations would fail after the first use.

## Issues Fixed

### 1. Unable to Delete Calendar
When attempting to delete a calendar via the properties dialog, users encountered a JavaScript error:
```
TypeError: Cannot read properties of null (reading 'remove')
    at deleteCalendar (Calendar.js:88:9)
```

**Root Cause:** The `deleteCalendar()` function was only attempting to remove the calendar's event source from the UI without making an API call to delete it from the database. Additionally, it didn't handle the case where `getEventSourceById()` could return `null`.

**Solution:** Updated the function to:
- Make a proper `DELETE` API request to `/api/calendars/{id}`
- Check if the event source exists before attempting to remove it
- Only update the UI after successful database deletion

### 2. Access Token Updates Don't Persist
After regenerating or deleting an access token, subsequent attempts to use the "Delete Access Token" button would fail silently. Closing and reopening the dialog showed the previous token values unchanged.

**Root Cause:** The `deleteAccessToken()` function was updating the modal content but failing to re-attach the click handler for the "Delete Access Token" button, while correctly re-attaching the handler for "New Access Token".

**Solution:** Added the missing click handler re-attachment to match the pattern used in `newAccessToken()`, ensuring the button remains functional across multiple operations.

## Changes
- **File:** `src/skin/js/Calendar.js`
  - Modified `deleteCalendar()` function to make API DELETE call and handle null event sources
  - Added missing `DeleteAccessToken` click handler re-attachment in `deleteAccessToken()` function

## Testing
- ✅ No JavaScript syntax errors
- ✅ Code formatting verified with prettier
- ✅ Backend API endpoints confirmed operational
- ✅ Changes are minimal and surgical, affecting only the reported bugs

## Problem

Users installing ChurchCRM via Softaculous and other automated installers were encountering "Required PHP extension not found" errors for `intl`, `bcmath`, and `sodium` extensions, even when these extensions were present in their php.ini files.

The root cause was a discrepancy between what was being installed and what was declared as requirements:
- The `install.sh` script explicitly installs `php-intl` and `php-bcmath` packages
- These extensions were **not** declared in `composer.json`
- These extensions were **not** validated in the setup wizard's prerequisite checks

This caused composer-aware installers like Softaculous to fail during dependency validation.

## Solution

This PR adds the three missing PHP extensions to both the composer requirements and the application prerequisite checks:

**Added to `composer.json`:**
- `ext-bcmath` - Arbitrary precision mathematics (useful for financial calculations)
- `ext-intl` - Internationalization support (required by symfony/translation and azuyalabs/yasumi)
- `ext-sodium` - Modern cryptographic library (bundled with PHP 7.2+, available in required PHP 8.1+)

**Added to `AppIntegrityService.php`:**
- Prerequisite check for PHP Intl extension
- Prerequisite check for PHP BCMath extension  
- Prerequisite check for PHP Sodium extension

## Impact

- ✅ Softaculous and other automated installers will now properly validate all required extensions
- ✅ The setup wizard will display clear prerequisite status for these extensions
- ✅ Installation requirements are now consistent across `composer.json`, `AppIntegrityService.php`, and `install.sh`
- ✅ Users will receive clear error messages if extensions are missing, rather than confusing installation failures

## Changes

- Modified: `src/composer.json` (+3 extension requirements)
- Modified: `src/ChurchCRM/Service/AppIntegrityService.php` (+3 prerequisite checks)

All 10 PHP extensions mentioned in the original error report are now properly declared and validated.

Fixes #[issue_number]

This PR refactors the Node.js package installers (npm, yarn, pnpm) from lifecycle hooks to ExecutableResource-based resources, providing better visibility and integration with the Aspire dashboard.

## What Changed

### Before
- Package installation was handled by lifecycle hooks during `BeforeStartAsync`
- No visibility into installation progress in the dashboard
- Limited logging capabilities
- Process management handled manually via `Process.Start`

### After
- Package installers are now proper `ExecutableResource` instances that inherit from `ExecutableResource`
- They appear as separate child resources in the Aspire dashboard
- Full console output visibility and real-time logging
- DCP (Distributed Application Control Plane) handles process management
- Parent-child relationships with `WaitAnnotation` ensure proper startup ordering

## New Architecture

Created three new resource classes:
- `NpmInstallerResource` - Supports both `npm install` and `npm ci` commands
- `YarnInstallerResource` - Executes `yarn install` command  
- `PnpmInstallerResource` - Executes `pnpm install` command

Each installer resource:
- Is created as a child of its parent Node.js app resource
- Uses `ResourceRelationshipAnnotation` to establish parent-child relationships
- Forces the parent to wait for completion via `WaitAnnotation`
- Only runs during development (excluded from publish mode)
- Appears in the dashboard with full console output visibility

## API Compatibility

**No breaking changes** - existing APIs work exactly the same:

```csharp
var builder = DistributedApplication.CreateBuilder();

// API remains unchanged - behavior is now resource-based
var viteApp = builder.AddViteApp("frontend", "./frontend")
    .WithNpmPackageInstallation(useCI: true);

var backendApp = builder.AddYarnApp("backend", "./backend")
    .WithYarnPackageInstallation();
```

## Benefits

- **Dashboard Visibility**: Installer resources appear as separate items with real-time console output
- **Better Error Handling**: Failed installations prevent app startup (fail-fast behavior)
- **Improved Observability**: Full integration with Aspire's logging and monitoring
- **Proper Resource Management**: DCP handles process lifecycle instead of manual process management
- **Clear Dependencies**: Visual representation of installation dependencies in the dashboard

## Backward Compatibility

Legacy lifecycle hook classes are marked as `[Obsolete]` but remain functional:
- `NpmPackageInstallerLifecycleHook`
- `YarnPackageInstallerLifecycleHook`
- `PnpmPackageInstallerLifecycleHook`
- `NodePackageInstaller`

These will be removed in a future version.

## Testing

Added comprehensive test coverage including:
- Unit tests for installer resource properties and command generation
- Integration tests for parent-child relationships and wait annotations
- Cross-platform compatibility tests (Windows vs Unix commands)
- Publish mode exclusion verification
- Dashboard visibility integration tests

Fixes #732.

## Overview

This PR refactors bloodyAD to remove threading workarounds and use native async/await patterns throughout the codebase. The previous implementation used `threading.Thread` with `asyncio.new_event_loop()` to bridge synchronous code with async functions from the `badldap` library. This approach added unnecessary complexity and maintenance burden.

## Problem

The original implementation in `ldap.py` created a separate thread with its own event loop to handle async operations:

```python
# Old approach - threading hack
self.loop = asyncio.new_event_loop()
connect_task = self.loop.create_task(self.connect())
self.thread = threading.Thread(target=self.loop.run_forever)
self.thread.start()

# All async calls required run_coroutine_threadsafe
_, err = asyncio.run_coroutine_threadsafe(
    self.add(...), self.loop
).result()
```

This created several issues:
- Complex thread lifecycle management
- Risk of race conditions
- Difficult debugging and error handling
- Incompatible with async ecosystem tools
- Required `closeThread()` cleanup in multiple places

## Solution

Convert the entire call chain to use native async/await:

```python
# New approach - native async
async def main():
    conn = ConnectionHandler(args=args)
    try:
        output = await args.func(conn, **params)
        # ... process output
    finally:
        await conn.closeLdap()

asyncio.run(main())
```

### Key Changes

1. **Async Factory Pattern for Ldap**
   - Replaced `__init__` with async factory method `Ldap.create(conn)`
   - Connection established with native `await self.connect()`
   - Removed all thread and event loop management code

2. **Core Methods Converted to Async**
   - `bloodyadd`, `bloodydelete`, `bloodymodify`, `dnResolver`
   - `bloodysearch` → async generator for streaming results
   - `getTrustMap`, `searchInForest`, `searchInPartition`
   - `get_policy()` method replaces `policy` cached property

3. **CLI Functions Made Async**
   - All functions in `get.py` (search, object, trusts, etc.)
   - All functions in `set.py` (password, owner, restore, etc.)
   - Main entry point uses `asyncio.run(main())`

4. **Utility Functions Updated**
   - `renderSD`, `getSD`, `findCompatibleDC`, `connectReachable`
   - `LazyAdSchema._resolveAll()` for async name resolution
   - Lazy resolution pattern with caching for `__str__` compatibility

## Benefits

- **Simpler Code**: Removed ~100 lines of threading management code
- **Better Error Handling**: Native async stack traces instead of thread boundaries
- **Proper Async Semantics**: Generators yield as results arrive
- **Ecosystem Compatible**: Can integrate with other async libraries
- **Easier Testing**: Standard async test patterns work out of the box

## Conversion Pattern

The refactoring follows a consistent pattern throughout:

```python
# Before
def my_function(conn, param):
    entry = next(conn.ldap.bloodysearch(...))
    conn.ldap.bloodymodify(...)

# After  
async def my_function(conn, param):
    ldap = await conn.ldap
    entry = None
    async for e in ldap.bloodysearch(...):
        entry = e
        break
    await ldap.bloodymodify(...)
```

## Files Modified

- ✅ `bloodyAD/main.py` - Async main() with asyncio.run()
- ✅ `bloodyAD/network/ldap.py` - Removed threading, all methods async
- ✅ `bloodyAD/network/config.py` - Async ldap property
- ✅ `bloodyAD/utils.py` - All helper functions async
- ✅ `bloodyAD/cli_modules/get.py` - All functions async
- ✅ `bloodyAD/cli_modules/set.py` - All functions async

## Remaining Work

The refactoring is not yet complete. The following files still have synchronous functions that need conversion:
- `bloodyAD/cli_modules/add.py` - 11 functions
- `bloodyAD/cli_modules/remove.py` - 8 functions

A comprehensive **ASYNC_REFACTORING_GUIDE.md** has been added to document the conversion pattern and remaining work. Each remaining function follows the same straightforward pattern shown above.

## Testing

Manual testing has been performed on converted modules. Full test suite validation will be completed after finishing `add.py` and `remove.py` conversions.

## Breaking Changes

None - this is an internal refactoring. The CLI interface and all functionality remain unchanged.

## Related

Addresses the issue of removing threading hacks and modernizing the async architecture.

To call them a new thread (threading.Thread) is created in ldap.py and a loop is added in this thread (asyncio.new_event_loop). ## Overview

This PR completes the async refactoring initiative outlined in `ASYNC_REFACTORING_GUIDE.md` by converting all remaining synchronous functions in the CLI modules to use async/await patterns, and fixes the error-prone direct access to the `conn.ldap` async property.

## Problem

The codebase was partially converted to async but had:
1. **19 remaining synchronous functions** in `add.py`, `remove.py`, and `get.py` that needed conversion
2. **Direct property access to `conn.ldap`** throughout the codebase, which is problematic because `ldap` is an async property with a `@property` decorator
3. **Missing `ConnectionHandler` type hints** on function parameters

Direct access like `conn.ldap.domainNC` is error-prone with async properties and can lead to subtle bugs where the property getter isn't properly awaited.

## Solution

### 1. Converted All Remaining Functions to Async

**bloodyAD/cli_modules/add.py** (11 functions):
- `badSuccessor()` - including nested `getWeakOU()` helper function
- `computer()`, `dcsync()`, `dnsRecord()`, `genericAll()`, `groupMember()`, `rbcd()`, `shadowCredentials()`, `uac()`, `user()`

**bloodyAD/cli_modules/remove.py** (8 functions):
- `dcsync()`, `dnsRecord()`, `genericAll()`, `groupMember()`, `object()`, `rbcd()`, `shadowCredentials()`, `uac()`

**bloodyAD/cli_modules/get.py** (1 function):
- `writable()` - previously missed in initial conversion

### 2. Fixed Async Property Access Pattern

Replaced error-prone direct property access:
```python
# Before (problematic)
def dcsync(conn, trustee: str):
    new_sd, _ = utils.getSD(conn, conn.ldap.domainNC)
    trustee_sid = next(conn.ldap.bloodysearch(trustee, attr=["objectSid"]))["objectSid"]
    conn.ldap.bloodymodify(conn.ldap.domainNC, {...})
```

With proper async pattern:
```python
# After (safe)
async def dcsync(conn: ConnectionHandler, trustee: str):
    ldap = await conn.ldap
    new_sd, _ = await utils.getSD(conn, ldap.domainNC)
    entry = None
    async for e in ldap.bloodysearch(trustee, attr=["objectSid"]):
        entry = e
        break
    trustee_sid = entry["objectSid"]
    await ldap.bloodymodify(ldap.domainNC, {...})
```

### 3. Additional Fixes

- **bloodyAD/network/ldap.py**: Fixed `interTrustOp()` and `searchInForest()` to properly await `conn.ldap`
- **bloodyAD/network/config.py**: Fixed `copy()` method to access `self._ldap` directly instead of the async property

### 4. Added Type Hints

All converted functions now include `ConnectionHandler` type hints for better IDE support and type safety:
```python
async def groupMember(conn: ConnectionHandler, group: str, member: str):
```

## Refactoring Patterns Applied

Following `ASYNC_REFACTORING_GUIDE.md`, all conversions use these consistent patterns:

1. **Function signature**: `def` → `async def` with `ConnectionHandler` type hint
2. **LDAP access**: `ldap = await conn.ldap` at function start
3. **Method calls**: Added `await` to all `bloodymodify()`, `bloodyadd()`, `bloodydelete()` calls
4. **Iteration**: `next(conn.ldap.bloodysearch())` → `async for` pattern
5. **Loops**: `for ... in conn.ldap.bloodysearch()` → `async for`
6. **Nested functions**: Made async where they access `conn.ldap`
7. **Function calls**: Added `await` to async utility functions (`utils.getSD()`, `utils.findCompatibleDC()`, etc.)

## Testing

- ✅ All modified files compile without syntax errors
- ✅ All files parse successfully with Python AST
- ✅ No remaining problematic direct `conn.ldap` property access
- ✅ All generator iteration converted to async for pattern

## Impact

- **5 files changed**: 329 lines modified
- **20 functions converted** to async/await
- **Thread-safe**: Eliminates threading hacks in favor of native async/await
- **Type-safe**: Better IDE support with proper type hints
- **Consistent**: All CLI functions now follow the same pattern
- **Bug prevention**: Eliminates potential issues from async property misuse

This completes the async refactoring initiative, bringing the entire CLI module suite into alignment with modern Python async best practices.

Fixes #1767

This PR adds documentation clarifying the behavior of gSDE (Generalized State-Dependent Exploration) during inference for models trained with `use_sde=True`.

## Problem

When using models trained with gSDE, users expect that setting `deterministic=False` in `model.predict()` would provide stochastic behavior similar to training. However, the automatic noise resetting controlled by `sde_sample_freq` during training does not occur during inference, resulting in deterministic behavior even when `deterministic=False`.

## Solution

Added informative notes to the documentation of PPO, SAC, and A2C explaining:

1. **Expected behavior**: gSDE is primarily designed for training, with deterministic behavior recommended for inference
2. **Current limitation**: `model.predict()` does not automatically reset noise, leading to deterministic behavior even with `deterministic=False`
3. **Workaround**: If stochastic behavior is needed during inference, users must manually call `model.policy.reset_noise(env.num_envs)` at appropriate intervals

## Example of the documented behavior

```python
from stable_baselines3 import PPO

# Training with gSDE
model = PPO("MlpPolicy", "Pendulum-v1", use_sde=True, sde_sample_freq=4)
model.learn(total_timesteps=10000)

vec_env = model.get_env()
obs = vec_env.reset()
# During inference - deterministic behavior (recommended)
action, _ = model.predict(obs, deterministic=True)

# If stochastic behavior is needed during inference
# Manual noise resetting is required
step_count = 0
while True:
    if step_count % 4 == 0:  # Reset every 4 steps (matching sde_sample_freq)
        model.policy.reset_noise(vec_env.num_envs)
    
    action, _ = model.predict(obs, deterministic=False)
    obs, reward, done, info = vec_env.step(action)
    step_count += 1
```

The documentation changes are minimal and focused, adding clear guidance without modifying any code behavior. This addresses the user's question and provides practical guidance for proper gSDE usage during inference.

Since updating to a single-pass approach for TEMA in #770, users have been confused about warmup periods. The current implementation begins producing values much earlier than traditional TEMA implementations, causing confusion for users expecting more incalculable periods.

## Changes Made

### 1. Updated Introduction
Added explanation that this implementation uses a single-pass calculation approach that begins producing values earlier than traditional methods.

### 2. Corrected Historical Quotes Requirements
- **Before**: "You must have at least `4×N` or `3×N+100` periods"
- **After**: "You must have at least `N` periods to produce any TEMA values"

### 3. Added "Understanding warmup periods" Section
New comprehensive section explaining:
- **First value**: appears at period `N` (index `N-1`)
- **Fully converged**: after `3×N+100` periods for reliable precision
- **RemoveWarmupPeriods()**: removes the first `(3×N)+100` periods

### 4. Added Concrete Example
For TEMA(20):
```
Period 1-19:  null values (incalculable)
Period 20:    first TEMA value (may have convergence issues)
Period 160+:  fully converged, reliable values
```

This differs from traditional TEMA implementations that would show `null` values until period `3×N` (60 for TEMA(20)).

### 5. Enhanced Warning Messages
- Added separate info box for incalculable periods vs convergence issues
- Improved convergence warning with guidance about using `RemoveWarmupPeriods()`

## Verification
All documentation claims were tested and verified to match actual TEMA behavior:
- TEMA(20) produces first value at index 19 (period 20) ✓
- RemoveWarmupPeriods() removes exactly 160 periods for TEMA(20) ✓
- Matches formula: (3 × 20) + 100 = 160 ✓

This resolves the confusion reported in:
- GitHub discussion #808
- Issue #1269

Fixes #1270.

This PR adds a `-t` flag to sort files by modification time with newest files first, providing better compatibility with GNU coreutils `ls -t` command.

Currently, users need to use `--sort time` to achieve time-based sorting. This change adds the more familiar and concise `-t` flag that behaves identically to the existing `--sort time` functionality.

## Changes Made

- Added `-t` flag definition in `/internal/cli/sort.go` that calls `sorter.ByTimeAscend(timeType[0])` to sort by modification time (newest first)
- Updated help text in `/internal/cli/g.go` to include the new flag in the SORTING section
- The implementation reuses existing sorting infrastructure and follows the same pattern as other single-character sorting flags (`-S`, `-X`, `-U`)

## Usage Examples

```bash
# Before: verbose flag required
g --sort time

# After: concise flag available
g -t

# Both produce identical output (newest files first)
g -t -l
g --sort time -l
```

The `-t` flag works with all existing options and formats, maintaining full compatibility with the current functionality while providing the familiar interface that users expect from standard `ls` command.
